content.value_statement: Teams lose context when completed work is not documented. This skill turns changes, impact, validation, and follow-up tasks into a structured completion report.
actual_capabilities: Defines a YYYY-MM-DD-title-report.md filename pattern under docs/reports.
Provides required sections for overview, changed files, detailed changes, validation, and follow-up tasks.
Classifies change types such as feature, fix, refactor, documentation, performance, security, breaking change, and deletion.
Includes Before and After, impact analysis, and Mermaid diagram sections for complex changes.
Guides collection of changed file names and verification results before writing the report.
limitations: It is a documentation template, not an automated report generator.
It does not validate project changes or test results by itself.
It may need translation if your team writes reports outside Korean or English.
It assumes reports are stored under docs/reports unless you adapt the filename rule.

use_cases.title: Record Implementation Outcomes
use_cases.description: Create a consistent report after a feature, fix, or refactor is complete.

use_cases.title: Prepare Review Handoffs
use_cases.description: Summarize changed files, validation results, impact, and remaining follow-up tasks for reviewers.

use_cases.title: Document Audit Work
use_cases.description: Capture security or quality changes with clear scope, evidence, and verification notes.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Completion Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after a small completed task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a completion report for this finished task. Include the change reason, changed files, validation results, and follow-up tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Changed Files Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you already know the affected files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a docs/reports report for these changed files. Classify each change type and explain the impact in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Migration Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for structural or workflow changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a migration completion report with Before and After sections, direct impact, indirect impact, preserved behavior, and validation evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Release Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before handing work to another team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a detailed release handoff report. Include decisions made, alternatives rejected, changed file groups, verification evidence, risks, and next actions.

output_examples.input: A refactor renamed a project folder and all validation passed.
output_examples.output: Report includes a date-based filename, rename reason, affected paths, Before and After comparison, validation summary, and follow-up checklist.

output_examples.input: A security audit fixed authentication checks and found one follow-up task.
output_examples.output: Report lists the security change type, modified files, test results, impact scope, and the remaining follow-up item.

output_examples.input: A documentation update changed setup instructions for a new release.
output_examples.output: Report explains the documentation scope, changed pages, review status, user impact, and remaining publishing steps.

best_practices: Write the report immediately after the task while details are fresh.
Include actual validation results instead of only saying the work was tested.
Keep follow-up tasks specific enough for another person to continue the work.
anti_patterns: Do not use the report as a replacement for tests or code review.
Do not omit impact analysis when files or behavior changed across modules.
Do not list changed files without explaining why each group changed.

faq.question: Does this skill execute shell commands?
faq.answer: No. It describes read-only git commands as workflow examples and depends on host tool permissions.

faq.question: Can I change the report folder?
faq.answer: Yes. Adapt the filename rule if your project stores reports outside docs/reports.

faq.question: Is this only for code changes?
faq.answer: No. It can document documentation, configuration, security, migration, and process changes.

faq.question: Does it create test evidence automatically?
faq.answer: No. You should provide the real validation commands, results, or review evidence.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What makes a good report title?
faq.answer: Use a short title that names the completed change, such as security-audit or path-renaming.
